content.title: Context: Reach Without Prop Drilling
content.hook: Sometimes a value genuinely belongs to a broad part of the tree.
content.context:
Passing it through many components that do not use it is called **prop drilling**.

Example:

```text
App
 ↓
Shell
 ↓
Panel
 ↓
Toolbar
 ↓
Button
```

Suppose only `Button` needs the current theme.

Passing `theme` through every middle component can become noisy.

React Context gives another option.
goals: Master Context: Reach Without Prop Drilling: “Many descendants belong to the same shared environment.”

content.title: The idea
content.text:
A provider makes a value available to components below it.

Conceptually:

```text
Theme provider
    ↓
Shell
    ↓
Panel
    ↓
Toolbar
    ↓
Button reads theme
```

The middle components do not have to forward the value.

content.question: Which is a good use case for Context?

options.text: One input value used by one nearby component
A theme value needed by many distant components in one UI tree

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. A theme value needed by many distant components in one UI tree
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. A theme value needed by many distant components in one UI tree

content.title: Before Context
content.text:
Context is powerful enough to be overused.

React's own guidance suggests considering ordinary props and component extraction before reaching for Context.

Ask:

1. Is the consumer actually far away?
2. Can a cleaner component boundary remove the prop drilling?
3. Does the value really describe a shared environment?

If the answer is no, Context may add more indirection than value.

content.title: Simple Context example

activities.title: Context is not automatically global state

content.title: Context is not automatically global state
content.text:
A provider can be placed around only part of the application.

That means Context can represent the scope of a concern.

For example:

```text
Application
├── Public area
└── Editor area
    └── EditorContext
```

The editor's state can stay scoped to the editor.

content.title: Reducer + Context
content.text:
You already learned reducers earlier.

At application scale, a reducer can define the update rules while Context makes the state and dispatch available to distant descendants.

```text
Provider
├── state
├── dispatch
└── child tree
```

That is one valid pattern for a complex client-side feature.

options.text: Context should be used for every shared value.
Context is useful when a value is needed deeply or broadly, but explicit props and composition are still valuable.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: C. Context is useful when a value is needed deeply or broadly, but explicit props and composition are still valuable.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: C. Context is useful when a value is needed deeply or broadly, but explicit props and composition are still valuable.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Context is not a shortcut around architecture.
Use it when the application's structure says:
**“Many descendants belong to the same shared environment.”**
nextSteps: Find one prop that travels through components that do not use it. Decide whether composition, a cleaner boundary, or Context is the best response. Explain your choice.

Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
